idea: Buy Apple every time it drops 5% in a week

spec.name: AAPL 5% weekly dip buy
spec.summary: Buy AAPL when it has fallen 5% over the last 5 trading days. Sell using a standard time limit since no exit was specified.
assumptions: Buys only when not already holding.
A 1-week drop means a 5-trading-day percent change.
Adds a 21-trading-day hold because no exit rule was provided.

idea: Same idea, but add an 8% stop-loss

spec.name: AAPL 5% weekly dip buy
spec.summary: Buy AAPL when it has fallen 5% over the last 5 trading days. Sell using a standard time limit since no exit was specified, and also use an 8% stop-loss.
assumptions: Buys only when not already holding.
A 1-week drop means a 5-trading-day percent change.
Adds a 21-trading-day hold because no exit rule was provided.
Adds an 8% stop-loss measured from the buy price.

idea: Buy the market when everyone panics (VIX above 30) and hold for three months

spec.name: Buy SPY on VIX panic
spec.summary: Buy SPY when VIX is above 30. Hold the position for three months, then sell.
assumptions: Uses daily close data and enters on the first day VIX is above 30 when not already holding.

idea: Sell in May and go away, buy back in November

spec.name: Sell in May, buy in November
spec.summary: Hold the selected market ETF during November through April and stay in cash from May through October. Enter in November and exit at the start of May.
assumptions: Uses calendar months only, with trades triggered by the current month's number on the close.
If already holding when May begins, exit on the first trading day of May.

idea: Buy Nvidia when its 50-day average crosses above its 200-day average, sell when it crosses back below

spec.name: NVDA 50/200-day moving average cross
spec.summary: Buy NVDA when its 50-day average crosses above its 200-day average. Sell when the 50-day average crosses back below the 200-day average.
assumptions: Uses closing prices to calculate both moving averages.
Only one NVDA position can be held at a time.

idea: Buy Tesla when RSI drops under 30 and sell when it gets above 70, with a 10% stop-loss

spec.name: TSLA RSI oversold to overbought
spec.summary: Buy TSLA when its RSI falls below 30. Sell when RSI rises above 70 or if the trade loses 10% from the entry price.
assumptions: Uses the standard 14-day RSI because no lookback was specified.
Signals are evaluated on daily closing prices.
The stop-loss is based on the close falling 10% below the buy price.

spec.reason: Nancy Pelosi’s trades require politician trade disclosures and individual stock transaction data, which are not available in the provided daily price data.
spec.closest: A testable proxy would be buying SPY when it is above its 200-day average and selling when it falls back below, or another single-ticker price-based rule using the available data.
